title: Which SQL Server CDC tool fits you?

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want a vendor to run the loads

options.label: My team runs it on our own servers
Microsoft Fabric runs it for me
options.why: you want Microsoft's platform to run it

questions.q: Where does the data have to land?

options.label: A warehouse
options.why: warehouses are among the targets these tools list

options.label: Iceberg tables on Amazon S3
options.why: your target is Iceberg on S3 (Fabric mirroring writes to OneLake)

options.label: Iceberg on Google Cloud Storage or Amazon S3 Tables
options.why: you want Iceberg on Google Cloud Storage or S3 Tables, which Striim's Iceberg writers cover

questions.q: What do your tables look like?

options.label: Many have no primary key
options.why: Estuary's CDC connector handles tables without a primary key, though you set a key by hand

options.label: CDC is not allowed on the server
options.why: CDC is off the table, so you need a method that skips it: Fivetran Teleport Sync, or Estuary's batch connector, which its docs say polls

options.label: They have keys and CDC is fine

questions.q: How fresh does the data need to be?

options.label: Continuous streaming
options.why: you need changes as they happen

questions.q: How often do columns get added?

options.label: Often, about monthly
options.why: Estuary and OLake Go both switch to a second capture instance

options.label: Rarely
options.why: new columns are rare, so Fivetran's single capture instance rule matters less

questions.q: How worried are you about load on the source server?

options.label: Very, it is big and busy
options.why: lower load (Striim's claim for MSJet) or a read from a replica matters to you

options.label: Not much
options.why: source load is not your main worry

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: A CDC engine with a free licence that reads SQL Server change tables and writes to Kafka topics, one per table.
debezium.bestWhen: Kafka is already in your stack.
debezium.watchOut: after an outage its docs warn of duplicate events, so your loads must cope with repeats.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run service that documents four ways to find SQL Server changes, including Teleport Sync for when CDC is off.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to run the pipeline and you are fine with billing on monthly active rows.
fivetran.watchOut: with CDC it syncs only tables with a single capture instance, so a new column means a new instance and removing the old one.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: Its Core edition is free to self-host under the Elastic License 2.0. The SQL Server connector uses CDC in scheduled syncs, with Iceberg on S3 through its S3 Data Lake destination.
airbyte.bestWhen: scheduled syncs are fine and you want something you can run yourself.
airbyte.watchOut: incremental CDC needs a primary key, delivery is at least once, and its CDC docs say it does not treat CDC sources as infinite streaming sources.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: Three SQL Server connectors: CDC, change tracking and batch, so you can pick the one that fits.
estuary.bestWhen: you want to choose between CDC and change tracking, or you have tables without a primary key.
estuary.watchOut: the CDC worker must run on the primary, and the batch connector polls, so expect latency of minutes to hours.

striim.name: Striim
striim.summary: Two readers: MS SQL Reader for CDC tables and MSJet for log backups, which Striim says uses less of the source server.
striim.bestWhen: you want to read log backups, and Striim's claim of lower load on the source matters to you.
striim.watchOut: its Iceberg Writer docs cover Google Cloud Storage, and its S3 Tables Writer covers Amazon S3 Tables.

fabric.name: Microsoft Fabric mirroring
fabric.summary: Microsoft's own way to copy a SQL Server database into Fabric.
fabric.bestWhen: Fabric is where your analysts work.
fabric.watchOut: data lands in Fabric OneLake as Delta tables, and a schema change breaks mirroring on 2016 to 2022 until you re-enable CDC for the table.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Our open-source tool. It reads SQL Server CDC capture instances (2017 or later) and writes Apache Iceberg or Parquet.
olake.bestWhen: you want SQL Server changes in Iceberg tables on storage you own and can run a container.
olake.watchOut: output is Apache Iceberg or Parquet, you run it on your own infrastructure, and it needs to keep reading inside SQL Server's three-day change table window (Microsoft's default).
